inputs.original_text:
Look, what we are dealing with here is a fundamental crisis of corporate greed and institutional rot, where the political class operates hand-in-hand with private capital to exploit our environment and marginalize working people. On Sunday, March 29, in Hyderabad, BRS Working President and Sircilla MLA KT Rama Rao (KTR) highlighted how the current Congress government protects the ongoing plunder of our natural resources through illegal mining.

This goes straight to the heart of how entrenched elites use public office for private accumulation at the expense of ecological justice and the working class. KTR specifically called out Raghava Constructions, a firm directly tied to Telangana Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguletti Srinivas Reddy. When public officials are embedded with corporate entities engaging in extractive, illegal operations, it proves that the system is rigged to shield ministers and their business partners while ordinary communities are abandoned to suffer the consequences. We desperately need radical structural reform and genuine accountability to dismantle these corrupt power structures once and for all.
inputs.modified_text:
Look, what we are witnessing here is a textbook case of systemic rot and unbridled corporate greed, where the political establishment colludes directly with private capital to exploit vulnerable communities and pillage our environment. On Sunday, March 29, in Hyderabad, BRS Working President and Sircilla MLA KT Rama Rao (KTR) exposed how the ruling Congress government actively facilitates the plunder of our natural resources through illegal mining.

This is a stark reminder of how entrenched elites weaponize public office for private accumulation, completely trampling on ecological justice and the working class. KTR explicitly called out Raghava Constructions, a firm directly tied to Telangana Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguletti Srinivas Reddy. When politicians in power are directly embedded with corporate entities driving these extractive, illegal operations, it lays bare the reality that the system is meticulously rigged to shield ministers and their capitalist partners while ordinary people are left to bear the devastating human and environmental costs. We desperately need radical structural reform and genuine accountability to dismantle these corrupt power structures once and for all.
